items.heading: If Daily Coding Drains
items.text: If daily coding drains you, the fix is not forcing yourself through five more years of it. The fix is building a skill portfolio that uses your engineering brain differently: structured thinking, comfort with technical detail, and the ability to turn a messy problem into a clear plan, without the requirement of writing and maintaining production code yourself.

items.heading: A Flat List of Job
items.text: A flat list of job titles is not useful by itself, because the same title means different things at different companies. Start with the underlying skill group, then look at which roles that skill group actually opens.

rows: Jira or Linear for backlogs, Figma for wireframes, Notion or Confluence for specs, and a simple one-page PRD template to practice writing requirements.
SQL (start with SELECT, JOIN, GROUP BY), Excel or Google Sheets for quick analysis, and Power BI or Tableau for dashboards once the SQL basics are solid.
Markdown plus a docs tool such as Confluence or a static-site generator, a public style guide like the Google Developer Documentation Style Guide, and a screen recorder for quick explainer clips.
Jira or Asana for tracking, a simple RAID log template for risk and dependency tracking, and PMP or CAPM study material once you already have real delivery experience to anchor it.
